strengths: Principled formulation: The paper clearly identifies a major limitation in existing cross-head KV cache allocation methods—namely, that raw heuristic score magnitudes are uncalibrated and correlate poorly with long-horizon utility across different attention heads. The formulation of global budget allocation as a discrete utility maximization problem solved via convex-hull relaxation (PAVA) and greedy allocation is sound and well-grounded.

Practically viable offline profiling: By discovering the empirical stability of head-wise marginal utility profiles across diverse tasks, the authors convert an expensive combinatorial optimization problem into an offline pre-computed lookup table. This avoids the memory spikes and runtime overhead of online dynamic sorting across layers (as seen in AdaKV).

Comprehensive and convincing evaluation: The method is evaluated across multiple modern LLMs (Mistral-7B-v0.3, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-32B) on both realistic multi-task benchmarks (LongBench) and stress-test synthetic retrieval (RULER 4K/16K). At aggressive compression rates (80%), LU-KV consistently and significantly outperforms Uniform, PyramidKV, and AdaKV baselines across three underlying eviction metrics (SnapKV, KeyDiff, EA).

Insightful analysis and ablations: The decomposition into oracle loss and the optimality gap (Eq. 7), supported by the ablation in Table 3 and visualizations in Figures 3, 4, and 6, clearly explains why existing heuristics suffer from 'loss bursts' in specific heads and deep layers.
weaknesses: Profiling dataset diversity and sensitivity: The offline calibration relies on a single synthetic narrative (~4,000 words) with 30 queries. While the resulting static profile generalizes well to LongBench and RULER, the paper does not explore sensitivity to calibration domain/length, nor does it evaluate whether calibrating on technical text, code, or mathematics would alter or further improve the allocation profile for domain-specific tasks.

Details regarding Oracle hyperparameters: In Eq. (4), Oracle Importance depends on a future decoding window parameter $K_{\max}$. The manuscript lacks details regarding the choice of $K_{\max}$, how sensitive the profiled utility curves are to varying $K_{\max}$, and the compute cost incurred during the offline profiling phase.

Hardware and kernel execution considerations: Modern LLM serving systems (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM) rely on uniform KV cache structures (often with PagedAttention or grouped-query attention). Because LU-KV produces non-uniform, head-wise variable cache lengths across layers, the paper would benefit from discussing the systems-level implementation challenges and showing autoregressive decoding throughput / token generation speedup alongside TTFT and memory footprint.

strengths: Sound and principled formulation: The paper clearly identifies the 'optimality gap' arising from using short-horizon heuristic scores across heterogeneous attention heads and formulates budget allocation as a global long-horizon utility maximization problem.

Elegant optimization approach: Using Isotonic Regression (PAVA) to compute a convex hull relaxation for discrete head-wise loss curves enables an exact and efficient greedy allocation scheme, providing a rigorous mathematical grounding for budget distribution.

Zero-overhead practical implementation: Leveraging the empirical observation that head-level utility allocation profiles remain structurally stable across tasks, the method precomputes allocation ratios offline, enabling an O(1) lookup during inference without the expensive cross-layer memory buffering required by dynamic sorting methods.

Comprehensive and convincing empirical validation: The framework is evaluated across three model architectures (Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-32B), three underlying eviction proxies (SnapKV, KeyDiff, Expected Attention), and two major benchmarks (LongBench and RULER). LU-KV demonstrates substantial improvements, especially under severe compression (80%).

Thorough diagnostics and ablations: Visualizations of layer-wise loss and head heatmaps (Figures 3 and 4) clearly explain why structural heuristics (PyramidKV) and score-based dynamic allocation (AdaKV) degrade, and the ablation in Table 3 directly supports the necessity of modeling the optimality gap.
weaknesses: Sensitivity and robustness of offline profiling data: The offline profile is constructed using a single AI-generated novel (~4,000 words) and 30 questions. The paper would benefit from a sensitivity study exploring how calibration data distribution (e.g., code, mathematical reasoning, multilingual text) impacts profile stability and downstream performance across specialized domains.

Missing comparisons with recent head-level baselines: Although recent allocation frameworks such as HeadKV (Fu et al., 2025) and CAKE (Qin et al., 2025) are discussed in the related work, they are not included in the empirical benchmark comparisons.

Hardware serving and memory fragmentation discussion: The paper demonstrates TTFT and peak memory reductions, but allocating heterogeneous cache budgets per head/layer can introduce memory fragmentation and non-uniform tensor layouts in modern PagedAttention / FlashAttention serving engines. A discussion or benchmark on autoregressive decoding throughput (tokens per second) and memory management overhead in practical serving frameworks would strengthen the systems aspect of the contribution.

Hyperparameter analysis of the oracle window: The oracle token importance definition relies on a maximum over future steps $K_{\max}$ (Eq. 4). The manuscript does not detail the exact value of $K_{\max}$ used during offline calibration or assess sensitivity to this horizon.

strengths: Sound conceptual framing: The paper clearly identifies a legitimate limitation in existing KV cache eviction methods—namely, that heuristic attention score magnitudes during prefill are uncalibrated across attention heads and do not correlate uniformly with true future utility (Oracle Importance).

Principled optimization framework: Formulating head-level budget allocation as a combinatorial optimization problem and solving its convex surrogate via Isotonic Regression (PAVA) and a greedy diminishing-returns solver is mathematically elegant and well-motivated.

Zero runtime optimization overhead: By observing empirical stability in head-wise compression profiles and computing a static lookup table offline, the method circumvents the substantial memory and latency overhead associated with online cross-layer/cross-head sorting.

Extensive empirical evaluation: The method is validated across three distinct open-weight LLMs (Mistral-7B-v0.3, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-32B) on both LongBench (16 datasets) and RULER (13 tasks), showing clear improvements over Uniform, PyramidKV, and AdaKV baselines at aggressive compression ratios (80%).
weaknesses: Omission of recent head-level allocation baselines: Although the related work explicitly mentions recent head-adaptive KV cache compression methods such as HeadKV (Fu et al., 2025) and CAKE (Qin et al., 2025), neither is included in the experimental comparisons in Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, or 7. Comparing only against Uniform, PyramidKV, and AdaKV makes it difficult to assess how LU-KV fares against state-of-the-art head-level pruning methods.

Calibration simplicity and cross-task profile variance: The offline calibration relies on a single synthetic narrative document (~4,000 words) and 30 generated QA pairs. While Figure 2b suggests general stability, the detailed head-by-head profiles in Figures 7–9 reveal non-trivial divergence across different task categories (e.g., code completion vs. retrieval vs. summarization). The paper lacks a sensitivity analysis evaluating how calibration data size, domain, and document length affect the learned profiles.

Unfulfilled benchmark claims: Section 5.1 explicitly states that RULER is utilized to evaluate contexts 'ranging from 4k to 128k tokens'. However, the manuscript only reports results for 4K (Table 7) and 16K (Tables 2 and 6), completely omitting results for 32K, 64K, or 128K context lengths.

Practical GPU memory layout and serving implications: In modern serving systems (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM) using PagedAttention or FlashAttention, allocating heterogeneous cache lengths $b(\ell, h)$ across individual heads can lead to memory fragmentation or require customized ragged/ragged-batch kernels. The paper does not discuss how variable-head budgets are practically handled in hardware without padding to the maximum head budget.

Sensitivity and definition of the Oracle Metric: The ground-truth oracle importance in Eq. (4) is defined using a $\max$ operator over the future decoding window $K_{\max}$. The paper does not provide an ablation or justification for choosing $\max$ over cumulative attention/output contribution (e.g., $\sum_k$), nor does it study sensitivity to the window size $K_{\max}$.

strengths: Insightful problem motivation: The paper identifies a clear limitation in existing KV cache budget allocation methods (e.g., PyramidKV, AdaKV), specifically that heuristic importance score magnitudes across different attention heads suffer from varying predictive fidelity relative to true future utility.

Principled and tractable optimization framework: Formulating head-level cache budgeting through marginal utility maximization, proving non-convexity, and applying isotonic regression (PAVA) convex relaxation allows for an exact, efficient greedy allocation with strong theoretical grounding.

Negligible runtime overhead: By discovering that head-wise compression profiles remain largely stable across downstream tasks, the method shifts the combinatorial optimization to an offline profiling phase, introducing zero online computational overhead during autoregressive decoding.

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation: The approach is thoroughly tested across diverse benchmarks (LongBench, RULER-4K/16K), model architectures (Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-32B), and multiple underlying token-scoring metrics (SnapKV, KeyDiff, EA, KVZip, CAKE), consistently demonstrating substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under high compression ratios (up to 80-90%).
weaknesses: Unclear handling of Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): All evaluated models (Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-32B) utilize GQA, where multiple query heads share a single KV head. The paper formulates attention output projection and budgeting over standard attention heads $(l, h)$ without clarifying whether budgets are assigned per KV head (aggregating over query heads) or if KV heads are duplicated/split.

Limited profiling diversity and sensitivity analysis: The offline profile is constructed using a single 4,000-token AI-generated Chinese novel and 30 questions. While Appendix F.2 shows reasonable transferability to an English SAT excerpt, deeper empirical exploration across diverse calibration domains (e.g., code repositories, multi-hop reasoning, technical documents) and calibration context lengths would better support the task-agnostic claim.

Hardware and serving system implications: While peak memory and TTFT are evaluated using KVPress, modern high-throughput serving systems (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM) rely on PagedAttention with uniform block allocation. The practical effects of non-uniform head budgets on memory fragmentation and customized attention kernel efficiency are not discussed.

strengths: Clear motivation and problem formulation: The paper identifies an important limitation in current KV cache eviction techniques—namely, that heuristic proxy scores across different heads have heterogeneous fidelity with respect to true long-horizon utility, rendering direct cross-head score comparisons suboptimal.

Theoretically sound relaxation: Formulating the head budget distribution as a discrete optimization problem, proving its non-convexity under heuristic ranking inversions, and applying isotonic regression via PAVA to establish a tractable convex surrogate solved by a greedy algorithm is well-derived and mathematically clean.

Comprehensive empirical validation: The framework is evaluated across multiple modern open-weight LLMs (Mistral-7B-v0.3, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-32B) on both LongBench and RULER benchmarks under aggressive compression (80% eviction), showing consistent gains across multiple underlying eviction metrics (SnapKV, KeyDiff, EA, KVZip, CAKE).

Practically efficient online execution: By decoupling budget profiling to an offline calibration phase, the online inference phase only requires an $O(1)$ table lookup, introducing virtually zero runtime computation or latency overhead.
weaknesses: Limited offline profiling diversity: The offline profile is constructed using a single 4,000-token synthetic text with 30 generated queries. While Appendix F.2 shows cross-corpus transferability to an English SAT snippet, calibrating on such a small corpus raises concerns regarding robustness across fundamentally distinct modalities or domains (e.g., multi-turn conversational agents, long codebases, or complex mathematical proofs).

Absence of decode throughput and kernel-level serving evaluation: Figure 5 reports peak memory usage and Time-To-First-Token (TTFT), but omits decoding throughput (tokens/second) during generation. In production serving systems (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM), non-uniform KV allocation across attention heads can introduce memory fragmentation or overhead in ragged PagedAttention kernels. Practical serving metrics should be reported.

Comparison with HeadKV in the main text: HeadKV also performs offline calibration for head-level KV budget allocation. However, comparison with HeadKV is relegated to Appendix F.3 under a specialized setting, rather than included as a core baseline alongside AdaKV and PyramidKV in Tables 1 and 2.

Justification of the Oracle Importance definition: Equation 4 defines the oracle metric strictly as the peak contribution $\max_{k} (A_{\ell,h,k,j} \|v_{\ell,h,j} W_O\|)$ across decoding steps. The paper does not thoroughly discuss or ablate why an extremum metric is preferable over cumulative or average attention mass across the decoding window, particularly for tokens that provide steady, moderate utility over many generation steps.

strengths: Principled Problem Formulation: The paper clearly identifies a major blind spot in existing cross-head KV cache eviction methods—namely, that heuristic importance scores have heterogeneous predictive fidelity across heads and layers, meaning magnitude does not equal true marginal utility.

Sound Theoretical and Algorithmic Framework: Formulating budget allocation as a combinatorial optimization problem over oracle importance and resolving the non-convexity via convex-hull relaxation (isotonic regression using PAVA) and a greedy diminishing-returns solver is mathematically elegant and well-motivated.

Negligible Online Overhead: By recognizing that head-wise utility curves exhibit stable cross-task patterns, the method reduces online allocation to a constant-time table lookup. This completely bypasses the runtime sorting overhead and memory spikes that plague dynamic allocation methods like AdaKV.

Extensive and Rigorous Empirical Evaluation: Evaluated across three distinct LLM architectures (Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-32B), two major long-context benchmarks (LongBench and RULER), and multiple intra-head eviction metrics (SnapKV, KeyDiff, EA, KVZip, CAKE). The performance retention under aggressive 80% and 90% compression ratios is consistently superior to baselines, showing remarkable gains on challenging RULER multi-needle tasks.

Thorough Analysis and Ablations: The appendix provides extensive per-dataset breakdowns, full head-wise profile visualizations across all 32 layers, transferability tests across differing calibration corpora, and an ablation on the optimality gap loss.
weaknesses: Handling of Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): All evaluated models (Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-32B) utilize GQA, where several query heads share a single KV head (e.g., 32 query heads vs. 8 KV heads in Mistral/Llama). In Section 3 and Eq. (4), the notation assumes a standard MHA architecture with head-specific output projections $W_O^{(\ell, h)}$. The manuscript should clarify how the oracle importance $I_{\ell, h, j}$ is aggregated across query heads sharing the same physical KV cache head.

Context Length Scaling during Profiling: The offline profile is constructed using a context length of $\approx 4,000$ tokens, yet evaluations extend up to 16k and 128k (RULER). While the empirical results are strong, the paper lacks an explicit discussion or empirical verification of whether the optimal local-to-global compression ratios remain scale-invariant when context length increases by orders of magnitude.

Profiling Cost and Metric Coupling: Because the allocation profile $\Phi^{(\pi)}$ depends on the specific intra-head metric $\pi$, any change to the scoring heuristic requires re-running the offline profiling phase. Reporting the exact wall-clock profiling runtime for large models (e.g., Qwen2.5-32B) would clarify deployment practicalities.
